question: In December 2024, India mourned the passing of Dr Manmohan Singh. In which year did Dr Manmohan Singh first become the Prime Minister of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2004**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dr. Manmohan Singh became the **13th Prime Minister of India** in May 2004, after the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) won the general elections.
 
• He was the first Sikh to hold the position of Prime Minister in India.
 
• Dr. Singh served two consecutive terms as Prime Minister from **2004 to 2014**.
 
• He succeeded **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**, who was the outgoing Prime Minister at the time.
 
• His tenure is noted for significant economic reforms and initiatives, including the continuation of liberalization policies introduced in the 1990s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dr. Manmohan Singh's Background:**

 
 
• Dr. Singh is an economist and academician who served as the **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India** from 1982 to 1985.
 
• He was the architect of India's economic liberalization as the **Finance Minister from 1991 to 1996** under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.
 
 
 
• **UPA Coalition:**
 
 
• The United Progressive Alliance (UPA) is a coalition of center-left political parties in India led by the Indian National Congress (INC).
 
• Dr. Singh was chosen as Prime Minister after the Congress President Sonia Gandhi declined the position.
 
 
 
• **Key Achievements of Dr. Manmohan Singh:**
 
 
• During his tenure, major schemes like the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)** and **Right to Information (RTI) Act** were implemented.
 
• He played a pivotal role in signing the **India-US Civil Nuclear Agreement** in 2008, which strengthened bilateral ties and India's energy security.
 
 
 
• **Economic Reforms:**
 
 
• Dr. Singh is widely regarded as the pioneer of India’s economic reform era, which began in 1991 to combat the balance of payments crisis.
 
• He introduced policies to liberalize trade, attract foreign investment, and reduce fiscal deficits, transforming India's economy into one of the world's fastest-growing.
